sources.toolchain:
[toolchain]
# @fb-only: path = "../../../third-party/rust-toolchain/rustup/current/basic"
# Pinned to the last known-good nightly. nightly-2026-07-30 (rustc 8ab9fdff5)
# changed cargo's cdylib artifact uplift under `cargo test`, so
# `target/debug/libreverie_examples.so` is no longer present when the
# reverie-examples liteinst integration tests run, breaking all reverie CI.
# Unpin once the cdylib/`cargo test` interaction is fixed upstream or the
# liteinst fixture is made robust to the artifact layout.
channel = "nightly-2026-07-29" # @oss-only
# Date-pinning installs a fresh dated toolchain; rustup only adds clippy/rustfmt
# for it when they are requested here (the unpinned `nightly` got them from the
# CI toolchain-setup action). Both shipped in the 2026-07-29 nightly.
components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"] # @oss-only

sources.toolchain:
[toolchain]
# @fb-only: path = "../../../third-party/rust-toolchain/rustup/current/basic"
# Pinned so the OSS Buck2 build is reproducible. The shim's Rust toolchain is
# `system_rust_toolchain`, which runs whatever `rustc` is on PATH; under rustup
# that resolves through this file, so a floating `nightly` gives a cold reviewer
# a different compiler on a different day and leaves every other bootstrap pin
# (Buck2 release, Reindeer revision) without effect. nightly-2026-07-12 is the
# toolchain used by the recorded Buck2 validation: rustc 1.99.0-nightly
# (be8e82435 2026-07-11). See docs/BUCK2_OSS.md.
channel = "nightly-2026-07-12" # @oss-only
# Date-pinning installs a fresh dated toolchain; rustup only adds clippy and
# rustfmt for it when they are requested here.
components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"] # @oss-only
